head: 9fc4ffa
target: Keep a secret the model streams across text-delta boundaries out of what listeners receive: the stream is now redacted as joined text, the way the transcript always was.
incidental: hoisting the merged secrets map into a const so the same value feeds the engine and the hold's size
the fauxSession test helper taking faux-provider options (and its type import) so tests can pace the provider

questions.prompt: Before this change, the adapter redacted each text delta on its own before it reached listeners. A secret the model wrote out across two deltas reached a listener whole, while the transcript and the RunResult stayed clean. Why the difference?

options.label: The stream path never ran redaction at all — only the transcript and RunResult paths did.
The provider splits text after the adapter has already redacted it, so the halves slip through in between.

Redaction only replaces whole secret values in the text it is given, and no single delta contained the whole secret — the transcript and the RunResult redact the joined text, so only the stream leaked.
Listeners received the raw transcript export, which keeps text blocks unredacted until the run ends.

key_points: redaction replaces whole secret values, and only in the text it is given — a fragment of a secret never matches
the secret existed only in the joined stream, and the adapter redacted each delta on its own, never the joined text
the transcript and the RunResult stayed clean because they redact the joined text on their own paths

questions.prompt: During a single assistant message, what resets the text the hold-back is holding, and why does a secret split across two text blocks of that same message still get caught?

options.label: Each text block flushes when it ends, and the redaction of the second block catches the whole secret.
Nothing but the message's end: pi emits no event between two text blocks of one message, so the halves stay in one buffer and are redacted as joined text.
Text blocks are separate assistant messages, so message_end fires between them and each block redacts whole.
The engine redacts each text block before pi streams it, so the seam never carries a fragment.

key_points: within a message, only the flush at message_end resets the held buffer — pushes accumulate into it
pi emits nothing between two text blocks of one message, so there is no seam event where a reset could or should happen
the halves accumulate in one buffer, so the text is redacted joined and the cut keeps covering the seam

questions.prompt: Walk one text delta through the hold-back once enough text has arrived. Why is holding back the last `longest - 1` characters exactly enough — why can no secret survive in what has already been emitted, and why is nothing held longer than the risk requires?
key_points: every push redacts the whole accumulated buffer as joined text, so any secret fully inside it is already replaced before the cut is taken
a secret that future deltas could still extend must begin within the last `longest - 1` characters; one that began earlier is already whole inside the buffer and thus replaced
a secret straddling the cut would have to be longer than the longest secret, so the emitted prefix never needs redoing
the held remainder is at most `longest - 1` characters — shorter than any secret — so nothing is held beyond what the risk requires

questions.prompt: Suppose a future pi upgrade stops emitting message_end when an assistant message ends aborted or errors (it still emits it when a message finishes normally). Which of these follow?

options.label: The tail of an aborted reply never reaches listeners as that reply's text: only message_end flushes the buffer, so the held characters just sit there.
A secret split across two separate assistant messages would now reach listeners whole, because the buffer no longer resets between messages.
If a later assistant message in the same session streams text, the stranded tail is emitted as the front of that message's first text delta.
The transcript and the RunResult would begin showing secrets that listeners see, because they share the stream path.

key_points: only message_end flushes the buffer, so an aborted or errored reply's tail is stranded — listeners lose it as that reply's own text
the stranded tail is not gone forever: the next message's first push emits it, misattributed to the wrong message

secrecy survives the missing flush — the unreset buffer is what keeps the joined redaction spanning the seam, so a cross-message split is still caught; the break is delivery and attribution, not redaction
the transcript and the RunResult are untouched: they redact their own joined text

questions.prompt: The cut lands between the two halves of a surrogate pair — an emoji the model streamed, say. Without the surrogate check in the hold-back, what does a host that writes each text delta straight to a terminal see?

options.label: Two replacement characters: one delta ends with an unpaired high half, the next starts with the unpaired low half, and each prints as one.
Nothing wrong — the terminal's output buffer rejoins the halves and the emoji renders once the second delta lands.
The first delta prints a blank and the emoji renders normally when the second arrives, replacing it.
The stream stalls at the cut until the pair is complete, so nothing partial is ever printed.

key_points: the cut would end one delta with a lone high surrogate and begin the next with its low half
each unpaired half is invalid output on its own, so the terminal prints one replacement character for each — the emoji becomes two
the check avoids it by moving the cut back one character, so the pair leaves in a single delta

questions.prompt: Before this change, every eval run whose model streamed a secret across two text deltas scored a leak, and none do now. Walk through the two new tests: what does each arrange so its pass cannot be an accident, and what exactly does each pin down?
key_points: the first test forces the split: the secret is longer than the faux provider's largest chunk (20 characters), so it can never arrive whole in one delta
it asserts the joined deltas equal the redacted whole text, and that no delta boundary falls inside a surrogate pair — the emoji tail arranges exactly that cut

the abort test paces the provider by timers so the abort lands mid-reply; it asserts the reply was truly cut short and the joined deltas equal what the transcript kept, pinning that the flush at message_end delivers the held tail even on an abort

the number moved because the eval runner joins deltas before scrubbing — per-delta redaction always leaked there; anything that re-broke the join (per-delta redaction again, a lost message_end, a cut stranding a surrogate) would move it back

questions.prompt: Months later a host reports that a session streamed a whole API key to its UI with this change in place. The session was created with an empty secrets map, and the model had read the key out of a file at runtime. Which of these hold?

options.label: The hold-back was protecting exactly what it was keyed to: an empty map means nothing is held back and nothing is redacted, so the stream passed the key through.
The bug this change fixed has regressed — per-delta redaction must be back.
That session's transcript shows the key unredacted too: stream and transcript share the same keyed redactor, so the gap is registration, not the stream path.
Had the key been registered in the secrets map at session start, the same hold-back would have covered the stream exactly as the redaction covers the transcript.

key_points: the hold is sized and the redactor keyed by the secrets map fixed at session start — an empty map makes the hold a pass-through
coverage is exactly the map: the transcript would show the key unredacted as well, so stream and transcript stay consistent and the gap is registration
the change has not regressed: registering the key at start would have covered both paths, and nothing about a runtime-read key ever reaches a redactor that never saw it
